understand.title: Real answers. Not just numbers.
understand.subtitle: Freelancer OS explains your finances in plain language. The questions you actually ask, answered automatically.

cards.title: What happened this month
cards.body: Income vs expenses vs your historical average. Know immediately if this was a strong month or a difficult one.

cards.title: Where your money is going
cards.body: Every transaction categorised automatically. Subscriptions, tools, travel, taxes, visible in one clear view.

cards.title: What is coming next
cards.body: Cashflow forecasts built from your actual patterns. Know if next month looks tight before it arrives.

cards.title: What to do about it
cards.body: Specific recommendations based on your real numbers. Not generic advice. Actions from your own financial data.

recognition.title: Most months don't look like the last one.
recognition.body: One month feels comfortable. The next, a client pays late and everything feels tight. You've got a spreadsheet you update sometimes. You're fairly sure things are okay, but fairly sure isn't the same as knowing.
items: I don't know if this month was actually good, or just felt good.
I have no idea where 400 euros a month quietly disappears to.
I can't tell if my business is growing, or I'm just busier.
The only time I really look at this properly is at tax time.

narrative.whyBothNeg: Income dips and above-average expenses occurred together in {count, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}. When both move at once, cashflow turns negative fast.
narrative.whyLowIncome: Income fell below your monthly average in {lowCount} of the {count, plural, one {# negative month} other {# negative months}}. Expenses were roughly normal — the problem was income.
narrative.whyHighExpenses: Expenses exceeded your typical level in {highCount} of the {count, plural, one {# negative month} other {# negative months}}. Income held steady — the problem was spending.
narrative.actionBuildReserve: Build a 2-month income reserve. A buffer absorbs the impact when income and expenses move against you simultaneously.
narrative.actionStabiliseClients: Stabilise your client pipeline. Retainer agreements, earlier invoicing, or building a 60-day payment buffer all reduce the impact of slow-income months.
narrative.actionExpenseCeiling: Set a monthly expense ceiling before the month starts. Review your recurring costs quarterly.
narrative.actionAutomateSurplus: All months are positive. Consider automating a fixed monthly transfer to lock in surplus before it gets spent.
narrative.stabilityImproving: Fewer negative months were detected in the second half of this period than the first. Cashflow is becoming more stable.
narrative.stabilityWeakening: More negative months occurred in the second half than the first. Cashflow stability is weakening.
narrative.stabilityUnchanged: The number of negative months has stayed consistent. Cashflow stability has not changed.
